The custom-error reverts decode (0xe7764c9e, 0x5796f78a, 0xc30a7bd7, 0x4fec3a61, SignerNotAuthorised; raw reverts 10 -> 3) and ecrecover's input is sha3(call.data[...]); the UpdatePrice event is still 'newPrice=mem[mem[64] len _90 - mem[64] + 32]' (line 287).

regressions.source: RedstoneConsumerNumericBase / RedstonePriceFeed: uint256[] memory valuesForDataFeed = new uint256[](uniqueSignersThreshold) and the loops over it
regressions.issue: Addresses inside and after the zero-init loop now contain '64 * mem[X + 160]', a word stored as the constant 1 just before the loop and never written in it; the old text had the constant offsets 352/384.
regressions.rule: Forward a memory word stored before a loop when no store in the loop can alias it (the loop's stores are at or above a pointer greater than that word), so the pointer floor after the loop stays constant.

improvements: Custom-error reverts decoded (raw reverts 10 -> 3); the two identical SignerNotAuthorised reverts after ecrecover merge into one (P12); ecrecover's input decoded; the '- 118 > calldata.size' check folded into the SafeMath.sub (Panic(17), same revert, evaluated before the 0x4fec3a61 check as before); serialize returns 'Array(len=..., data=...)' for its bytes value; P2 54 -> 0 by the header's count; 54 fewer lines.
notes: Diff of 142 lines read in full. Old/new order of failing checks compared (Panic(17) checks may swap: same revert data).
summary: One minor regression: addresses around the zero-init loop carry '64 * mem[X + 160]' instead of constants. Otherwise better: custom errors and ecrecover decoded, duplicate reverts merged, serialize's bytes return wrapped.
